notes: Vela v1.0 — the 1.0 milestone. The shell is async by default: a foreground app runs cooperatively alongside background services on one event loop and one terminal, with the classic synchronous shell kept as the crash/recovery fallback. HTTPS now works on a device that has been running a while — the failure was never a shortage of free memory but of CONTIGUOUS memory, and meminfo reports the largest allocatable block so the difference is visible. Update checks follow the channel of the build you are running. Also: a full async line editor with history and Tab completion, background services (httpd --bg, the service manager), safeboot for staging a memory-heavy update, streamed package installs, and the recovery toolkit. Verified on Pico 2 W and ESP32-S3.
features: Async by default — background services keep running while you use the prompt (asyncmode off returns the classic shell)
Cooperative app framework (appkit) — foreground apps yield so services keep ticking
Full async line editor — history, Tab completion, cursor and word navigation
Background services — httpd --bg, the service manager, services.cfg
HTTPS works after the device has been up a while — the contiguous block a TLS handshake needs is claimed at boot and handed back when memory gets tight
meminfo reports the LARGEST ALLOCATABLE BLOCK and a fragmentation percentage, not just free memory
defrag — reclaim and report whether there is enough contiguous RAM for HTTPS
safeboot [cmd] — stage an update to run on a serviceless maintenance boot with full RAM
Update checks follow the channel of the build you are running; a differing build id can no longer offer an older version as an upgrade
pkg install streams the archive to flash — no MemoryError on large packages
Async networking — ping/wget/curl (incl. HTTPS) yield to the loop
Recovery — fscheck, diag, logdump, regreset, pkgdisable
